title: Hook a Club across a steering wheel and pull it snug
instruction: Lock the steering wheel with the Club across it, its handle pointing up, and let go of it.
context: Why: bar steering-wheel locks like the Club are the best-known car anti-theft device, back in wide use since the Kia and Hyundai thefts; most drivers have fitted one or watched one fitted. In a car the instrument hood and the windshield sit just behind and above the wheel's top, so the 558 mm bar is swung in under them from the driver's seat. The maker's guide: put one hook on first, then pull the other until it fits snugly; either hook may go first. The hooks open toward the bar's ends, so the lower hook can carry the 1.6 kg Club on the bottom of the grip but the upper one can't: hook the top first and one hand must hold the whole Club up with that hook seated while the other pulls the sliding half down. The knack is the pull: along the bar's line, the first hook kept seated, right through to the tooth at the grip. Stop more than 2.4 mm before the second hook meets the grip and the ratchet holds it a tooth short: it rattles loose. Done by: drivers locking a parked car.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y to the robot's left), heights above the table top. Wheel stand, clamped to the table with two 150 mm C-clamps: an 18 mm birch-plywood base board (x 45 to 86, y -30 to 30), a post on it (x 47 to 61, 9 cm tall), and a 100 mm square plywood box column running from the post up and back toward the robot at 25° above horizontal to a fixed steel hub stub. On the hub, with a Grant 3196 installation kit (the 3-bolt adapter for 1969-94 GM columns), a Grant Elite GT 742 steering wheel (14 in, 356 mm across, 3.75 in dish), black leather-grained vinyl grip 26 mm thick (inner diameter 304 mm), its four aluminium spokes meeting the grip at about 1:30, 4:30, 7:30 and 10:30, so 12 and 6 o'clock are clear. The wheel is fixed and does not turn (as a parked car's steering lock holds it). Its centre is at (30, 0), 20 cm up; its face leans back 25° from vertical like a car's, so the top of the grip is at x 37, 35 cm up, and the bottom at x 23, 5 cm up. The car around it, part of the stand: a dark-grey plywood dash 60 cm across, its upper part (from 25 cm up to its top, 4 cm above the top of the wheel) with its face 130 mm behind the grip at 12 o'clock (x 52), the lower part set back to x 56, both running back to x 85; on it a black instrument hood 36 cm across, 15 cm deep, its top 8 cm above the top of the wheel; and a windshield of 6 mm clear acrylic, 80 cm across and 50 cm up its slope, its lower edge on the dash 445 mm ahead of the wheel's top (x 82, 40 cm up), rising toward the robot at 37° from horizontal to x 42, 70 cm up. Fitted with its handle up, the Club clears the glass by about 4 cm and the hood by about 11 cm. The Club: Winner International The Club 1000 steering wheel lock, heat-treated steel with red vinyl-coated hooks and handle, 1.6 kg (outer piece 1.2 kg, inner 0.4 kg), 558 mm long closed. The outer piece is a 25 mm tube carrying the lock body, the upper hook and the handle, which runs 30 cm past that hook. The inner piece is a 19 mm bar with the lower hook; it slides out of the tube on a self-locking ratchet: it pulls out against a 5 N drag, clicks past a tooth every 4.8 mm and never slides back. Each hook is a 15 mm rod bent into a U that opens toward its own end of the bar: 38 mm from the bar to the lip, the lip 22 mm long. The hooks are 244 mm apart inside with the inner bar pushed in, and open to 415 mm. Start: the inner bar pushed fully in; the Club stands on its two hooks (hooks down) with the middle between the hooks at about (15, 8), the handle end to the robot's left and turned 30° toward the wheel (seen from above, the bar runs 30° clockwise from the y axis). Both arms start in their ready pose. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Judged at the end of the run with a steel rule, a protractor and the trial video. Hook on: the grip passes through that hook's U, the lip behind the grip and the bar in front, with the hook's stem within 10 mm of the grip's inner edge (real check: a 10 N pull toward the driver on that end moves it less than 5 mm). Play: with the Club resting on its lower hook, the gap between the upper hook's stem and the grip's inner edge, read with the steel rule (the 304 mm inner diameter less the hooks' inside spacing). Snug: play 4.8 mm or less, one tooth. Pulled until its lower hook meets the grip, this Club rests on the tooth that leaves 2.4 mm; a tooth short leaves 7.2 mm. Handle up: the handle within 30° of 12 o'clock, read with a protractor on the wheel's face. Released: both grippers 30 mm or more from the Club. Still: the Club (its upper hook, its handle end and the inner bar's travel) moves less than 1 mm over the last 1 s, with the grippers released throughout. Score 0 if the wheel stand moves more than 10 mm at any time, even if put back. Otherwise, at the end, the first that fits: 1.0 both hooks on, snug and the handle up, released and still; 0.75 both hooks on and snug, released and still, but the handle more than 30° from 12 o'clock; 0.5 both hooks on, released and still, but loose (play over 4.8 mm); 0.25 one hook on, released and still (the Club caught on the grip by one hook); 0 anything else, including the Club still held, dropped, on the table, or the untouched start. Either hook may go on first. The ratchet can't be pushed back, so only drawing the two halves apart (pulling the inner bar out, or pushing the outer piece up) makes a loose Club snug. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once 1.0 has held 1 s; only the end counts.
run_limit: 2,400 steps (2 minutes at 20 Hz); the scripted two-arm demo reaches 1.0 in 38 s (760 steps)
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Unlock the Club with its key, push the inner bar fully in, lift the Club off the wheel and stand it on its two hooks at its start marks. Check the stand and both C-clamps on their marks. Before the first trial of the day: read the inner bar's drag with a 20 N spring scale pulling it out (5 N, within 1 N), then fit the Club snug by hand and read the play at the upper hook (2.4 mm on this unit and wheel; record it if another unit's teeth fall differently). Run the simulator with -E object_jitter=0 (one fixed layout).
fidelity: Rigid bodies. Club and wheel at real size; masses, drag and pitch are estimates. The wheel is fixed. The grip is 40 straight square-section pieces; the tubes are square. The ratchet is one rule: the inner bar's slide-back limit follows the last 4.8 mm tooth it passed. Its 5 N drag is joint friction, static = sliding. Hooks hold the grip by contact alone. The car is a simplified stand-in: flat dash, hood and windshield panels in the stand's 30 kg free body, the hood 130 mm behind the grip.
